text: Paul and Timotheus, the servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus which are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons:
But I would ye should understand, brethren, that the things
Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
But I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timotheus shortly unto you, that I also may be of good comfort, when I know your state.
Finally, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed
Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision.
Therefore, my brethren dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord,
But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that now at the last your care of me hath flourished again; wherein ye were also careful, but ye lacked opportunity.
Salute every saint in Christ Jesus. The brethren which are with me greet you.
It was written to the Philippians from Rome by Epaphroditus.
